title: Verb + to-infinitive or bare infinitive
summary: Когда после глагола нужен инфинитив с to, а когда без to: модальные, make / let / have / help, глаголы восприятия (see + obj + V), had better, would rather, do nothing but, а также пассив make и let.
ru:
## Голый инфинитив (без to)
Инфинитив без **to** стоит после:
- **модальных глаголов**: can, could, may, might, must, should, will, would, shall.
- **had better, would rather, would sooner**: You **had better leave** now. / I'd **rather stay** at home.
- **let, make, have (в значении «поручить, попросить сделать») + дополнение**: She **made me redo** the report. / They **let us leave** early. / I **had the technician check** the wiring.
- **глаголов восприятия + дополнение** (see, hear, watch, notice, feel): I **saw him cross** the street.
- **why (not)**: **Why not ask** her directly? **Why wait**?
- **help**: можно с to и без: She **helped me (to) find** a flat.

## make, let, have: оттенки
- **make sb do** — принуждение: She **made me wait** for an hour. В пассиве **to возвращается**: I **was made to wait**. ~~I was made wait.~~
- **let sb do** — разрешение. У let + инфинитив пассива нет, его заменяет **be allowed to**: We **were allowed to leave**. ~~We were let leave.~~
- **have sb do** — поручить, организовать (AmE чаще, формально): I **had** the assistant **book** the tickets. **get sb to do** — то же, но разговорно и **с to**: I **got** the assistant **to book** the tickets.
- **help sb (to) do** — оба варианта правильны; без to чаще в американском английском.

## Глаголы восприятия: bare infinitive или -ing
Между **see him cross** и **see him crossing** есть разница.
> I **saw him cross** the road. — Я видел, как он перешёл дорогу целиком (законченное действие).
> I **saw him crossing** the road. — Я видел, как он переходил (в процессе, я мог увидеть не всё).
В пассиве после see / hear возвращается **to**: He **was seen to cross** the road. (Но с -ing: He was seen crossing.)

## to-infinitive: «глагол + дополнение + to»
Многие глаголы требуют **дополнение + to-infinitive**: **want, ask, tell, order, advise, allow, permit, enable, encourage, force, persuade, remind, warn, expect, invite, teach**.
> She **advised me to apply**. — The doctor **ordered him to stay** in bed. — They didn't **allow us to take** photographs.
Отрицание: **not to** — He told me **not to wait**.
Сравните: **want sb to do**, но **make sb do**. ~~She made me to wait.~~ → She made me **wait**.

## Особые случаи
- **do nothing but / cannot but + bare infinitive**, но **have no choice but to** (с to): He did **nothing but complain**. / I had **no choice but to accept**.
- **All I did was (to) ask…**, **What I want to do is (to) leave** — to можно опускать.
- **rather than**: **Rather than wait / to wait**, we walked. Допустимы оба варианта.
- **dare**: как модальный — без to: *I daren't say anything*; как обычный — с to или без него: *She didn't dare (to) speak*.
- **Split infinitive** (**to fully understand**) нарушает старое правило, но в современном английском допустим.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She made me to cry.~~ → She made me **cry**.
- ~~I let him to go.~~ → I let him **go**.
- ~~You'd better to leave.~~ → You'd better **leave**.
- ~~I'd rather to stay.~~ → I'd rather **stay**.
- ~~I saw him to leave.~~ → I saw him **leave** (в пассиве: He was seen **to leave**).
en:
## Bare infinitive
We use the infinitive **without to** after:
- **modal verbs**: can, could, may, might, must, should, will, would, shall.
- **had better, would rather, would sooner**: You **had better leave** now. I'd **rather stay** at home.
- **let, make, have (= arrange) + object**: She **made me redo** the report. They **let us leave** early. I **had the technician check** the wiring.
- **verbs of perception + object**: I **saw him cross** the street.
- **why (not)**: **Why not ask** her? **Why wait**?
- **help**: with or without to: She **helped me (to) find** a flat.

## make, let, have
- **make sb do** = force: She **made me wait**. In the passive **to returns**: I **was made to wait**.
- **let** + infinitive has no passive; we use **be allowed to**: We **were allowed to leave**.
- **have sb do** = arrange (more AmE): I **had** the assistant **book** the tickets. **get sb to do** is similar but informal and takes **to**.
- **help sb (to) do**: both forms are correct.

## Perception verbs: bare infinitive or -ing
> I **saw him cross** the road. (the whole action)
> I **saw him crossing** the road. (in progress)
In the passive **to** is used after see and hear: He **was seen to cross** the road.

## Verb + object + to-infinitive
**want, ask, tell, order, advise, allow, permit, enable, encourage, force, persuade, remind, warn, expect, invite, teach**: She **advised me to apply**. He told me **not to wait**. Compare: **want sb to do**, but **make sb do**.

## Special cases
- **do nothing but / cannot but + bare infinitive**: He did **nothing but complain**. But **have no choice but to accept**.
- **All I did was (to) ask**, **What I want to do is (to) leave**.
- **rather than** + bare infinitive or to-infinitive.
- **dare**: as a modal, bare (*I daren't say*); as an ordinary verb, with or without to (*She didn't dare (to) speak*).
- The split infinitive (**to fully understand**) is acceptable today.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She made me to cry.~~ → She made me **cry**.
- ~~I let him to go.~~ → I let him **go**.
- ~~You'd better to leave.~~ → You'd better **leave**.
- ~~I'd rather to stay.~~ → I'd rather **stay**.
structure:
## Без to
| После | Формула | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Модальные | modal + V | You must leave. |
| had better / would rather | + V | I'd rather walk. |
| make / let / have | + obj + V | She made me wait. |
| see / hear / watch / notice | + obj + V (весь процесс) | I saw him cross. |
| why (not) | + V | Why not ask? |
| do nothing but | + V | He did nothing but complain. |

## С to
| После | Формула | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| want / expect / ask / tell | + obj + to V | She told me to wait. |
| advise / allow / force / persuade | + obj + to V | They allowed us to go. |
| be made / be seen / be heard | passive + to V | He was made to wait. |
| have no choice but | + to V | I had no choice but to stay. |
| get | + obj + to V | I got him to help. |

## Актив → пассив
| Актив | Пассив |
|---|---|
| They made him wait. | He was made to wait. |
| They let him go. | He was allowed to go. |
| I saw her leave. | She was seen to leave. |
| I saw her leaving. | She was seen leaving. |

exercises.title: to или без to?
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол в скобках в нужную форму (с to или без to).
exercises.example: She encouraged him (apply) for the job. → She encouraged him **to apply** for the job.

items.text: The manager made everyone {{work}} late on Friday.
My parents let me {{stay}} up till midnight.
We were made {{to wait}} outside in the cold.
I'd rather {{walk}} than take the bus.
She advised him {{to see}} a specialist.
You'd better {{not tell}} anyone about this.
They didn't allow us {{to take}} photographs.
He did nothing all day but {{complain}}.
I had no choice but {{to accept}} their offer.
Rather than {{wait|to wait|waiting}} for the bus, we decided to walk.
The new software enables users {{to edit}} documents offline.
I'd sooner {{resign}} than work for him.

items.q: The coach made the players ___ ten extra laps.

items.why: После **help + object** — инфинитив (с to или без to).

items.q: The teacher let the students ___ the room early.
He was seen ___ the building at midnight.
items.why: В пассиве после see возвращается **to**: was seen **to enter**.

items.q: My boss told me ___ the file immediately.
We'd better ___ now, or we'll miss the train.

options: I was made to wait for an hour.
I was made wait for an hour.
I was made waiting an hour.

items.q: She didn't dare ___ him the truth.
items.why: После **didn't dare** to можно опустить: didn't dare **tell** = didn't dare to tell; -ing и V2 здесь невозможны.

items.q: The doctor ordered him ___ in bed for a week.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово в скобках.

items.prompt: The teacher forced us to rewrite the essay. (make) → The teacher ...
answers: The teacher made us rewrite the essay.

items.prompt: My father allowed me to borrow his car. (let) → My father ...
answers: My father let me borrow his car.
He was made to apologise.
He was made to apologize.

items.prompt: Her parents didn't let her go to the party. (allow) → Her parents ...
answers: Her parents didn't allow her to go to the party.
Her parents did not allow her to go to the party.

items.prompt: It's better for you to leave now. (had better) → You ...
answers: You had better leave now.
You'd better leave now.

items.prompt: I prefer to cycle rather than drive. (would rather) → I ...
answers: I would rather cycle than drive.
I'd rather cycle than drive.

items.prompt: I saw him. He opened the safe. (одно предложение с see, всё действие) → I saw ...
answers: I saw him open the safe.

items.prompt: He wasn't allowed to speak. → They didn't let ...
answers: They didn't let him speak.
They did not let him speak.

items.prompt: The only thing he did was complain. → He did nothing ...
answers: He did nothing but complain.

items.prompt: Она помогла мне найти квартиру. (help / flat)
answers: She helped me find a flat.
She helped me to find a flat.
She helped me find an apartment.
She helped me to find an apartment.

items.prompt: Они заставили меня ждать час. (make / wait / an hour)
answers: They made me wait for an hour.
They made me wait an hour.

items.prompt: Лучше не говорите ей. (had better / tell her)
answers: You'd better not tell her.
You had better not tell her.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя конструкции юнита.

items.prompt: Что вам в детстве не разрешали делать? (My parents didn't let me ...)
items.sample: My parents didn't let me watch TV on school days.

items.prompt: Что вас заставляли делать в школе? (I was made to ...)
items.sample: At school I was made to wear a uniform.

items.prompt: Чем вы предпочли бы заняться вместо чего-то другого? (I'd rather ... than ...)
items.sample: I'd rather read a book than watch a film.

items.prompt: Какой совет вы дали бы другу? (You'd better ...)
items.sample: You'd better start preparing for the exam now.

items.prompt: Кто вам помог в трудной ситуации? (helped me ...)
items.sample: My brother helped me move to a new flat.

items.prompt: Что вы видели или слышали на улице сегодня? (saw / heard + obj + verb)
items.sample: I heard a child sing in the courtyard this morning.
